Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates marked volume loss of the right lung with ipsilateral mediastinal shift and a characteristic kinked or anomalous vessel in the right cardiophrenic angle, which are classic radiographic signs of right upper lobe pulmonary hypoplasia (often associated with scimitar syndrome variants or isolated hypoplasia).
